steps.label: Loops and Pong
steps.content:
Year 6 Scratch

Loops and Pong

Year 6, 6.2.2

  • Repeat blocks with repeat and forever loops.
  • Make decisions with if and touching.
  • Build a Pong game that checks itself.

steps.label: Loops Repeat Blocks
steps.content:
Loops Repeat Blocks

A loop runs the blocks inside it again and again, so you only write them once.

  • repeat (4) runs the blocks inside it 4 times, then carries on below.
  • forever runs the blocks inside it until the game stops. Nothing goes underneath it.
  • A game keeps moving and checking because its scripts are inside forever loops.
repeat (4)
move (100) steps
turn left (90) degrees
end

forever
move (5) steps
if on edge, bounce
end

steps.label: Check: Count the Loop
steps.content:
Check: Count the Loop

Follow the loop one turn at a time.

when flag clicked
set x to (0)
repeat (5)
change x by (20)
end
Total: 2 marks

steps.label: Activity 1: Square Dance
steps.content:
Activity 1: Square Dance

Work on your own. Use a repeat loop to fly the Bee round the square.

Build it

  • The green flag sends the Bee to the start and points it right.
  • It flies round the dashed square, anticlockwise.
  • The moves sit inside one repeat block, and one lap takes at least a second.

The panel beside TurboWarp lists the checks. Press Check my project as often as you like: it plays your game and tells you what it saw.

steps.label: Sensing and If
steps.content:
Sensing and If

A condition is a question with a true or false answer. An if block runs its blocks only when the condition is true.

  • touching [Paddle]? is true while the Ball touches the Paddle.
  • Inside a forever loop, the if block checks again and again.
  • mouse x reports how far left or right the mouse is.
  • if on edge, bounce turns a sprite round at the edge.
when flag clicked
forever
set x to (mouse x)
end

if <touching [Paddle v] ?> then
change [score v] by (1)
end

steps.label: Check: Sensing and If
steps.content:
Check: Sensing and If

Choose the best answer.

items.prompt: Why is set x to (mouse x) inside a forever loop?
options: So the Paddle keeps following the mouse
So the Paddle moves only once
So the game stops at the floor
items.explain: Without the loop the Paddle would move once, when the flag is clicked, and never again.

items.prompt: The Ball is not touching the Paddle. What does touching [Paddle]? report?
items.explain: A condition is true or false. Not touching means false, so the if block skips its blocks.

steps.label: Pong Toolkit
steps.content:
Pong Toolkit

Two blocks you will need for Pong that you have not used before.

point in direction ((180) - (direction))
move (5) steps

Bounce off the Paddle

180 take away the direction flips the Ball from heading down to heading up. Moving 5 steps lifts it clear, so one hit counts once.

wait until <touching color [#e02424] ?>
stop [all v]

Game over at the floor

Click the colour square, then click the red floor on the stage to pick its colour. The script waits until the Ball touches red, then stops everything.

steps.label: Activity 2: Pong
steps.content:
Activity 2: Pong

Work on your own. The starter project has the Paddle, the Ball and a red floor.

Build it

  • The mouse moves the Paddle left and right.
  • The Ball starts at the top, keeps moving and bounces off the walls.
  • A hit bounces the Ball up and adds 1 to score. The green flag sets score to 0.
  • Touching the red floor stops the game.

The panel beside TurboWarp lists the checks. Press Check my project as often as you like: it plays your game and tells you what it saw.

steps.content:

steps.label: Checked Practice (2 of 2)
steps.content:
Checked Practice (2 of 2)

This is the Ball's scoring script. score starts at 0.

when flag clicked
forever
if <touching [Paddle v] ?> then
change [score v] by (1)
end
end
Total: 1 mark
